snippet.title: Computational Skepticism: Ten Multiple-Answer Questions
snippet.description:
Computational Skepticism: Ten Multiple-Answer Questions

Computational Skepticism exam preparation. Current instructor-specified format: five case-style questions at 10 points each and ten multiple-answer questions at 5 points each, totaling 100. Each case asks five specific questions, scored 3/2/2/2/1, rather than an open-ended essay.

Practice Project instructions are a local draft, not yet published or tested in a live Claude Project. The walkthrough shows a source-based workflow illustration, not a recorded live Claude session. Embedded starter notes allow practice without extra uploads. The narrower compact-list topic scope is used conservatively while conflicting scope documents await instructor resolution. No real exam or private answer key is shown.

Public course book:
https://github.com/nikbearbrown/info-7375-computational-skepticism-for-ai

Exam-prep playlist:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLelOldL5q7F0

The updated prompt remains local; a direct published prompt link is not available yet. Narration: Liam, a synthetic voice, in for Bear. Native 4K master.
